commands.name: tab_open
commands.description: Opens an address in a new tab.

args.name: url
args.meaning: An http or https address, on CHROME_ALLOWED_PREFIXES if that is set.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": this command has no background mode.

example_requests: Open example.com in a new tab
Load this page in a new tab
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: A new tab shows the page.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or a page didn't finish loading in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a field holds typed text, the Find bar has focus, a dialog can't be closed safely, or another app came to the front; nothing is changed

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode is "background", or the command wasn't verified

errors.name: UrlNotAllowed
errors.when: the address isn't http or https, or isn't on CHROME_ALLOWED_PREFIXES; nothing is done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with Chrome 157 against a local test server only, so macOS 26 and real websites aren't covered.
There is no background mode, because Chrome's scripting needs an Automation permission that wasn't granted.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Dialogs raised by a page, such as JavaScript's confirm, weren't tested.
The url returned is as Chrome's field shows it, usually without https://.
An address that redirects, or that Chrome shows differently from how it was given, can make the command time out with UIError after the page has loaded.
If the Find bar has focus, the command raises StateBlocked, because Accessibility then shows only the Find bar.
It turns on Chrome's AXEnhancedUserInterface setting, which stays on until Chrome quits.
With many tabs in one window (69 in a re-test), it could miss tabs or the active tab while Chrome was minimized or behind another app.
